transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, I came in because there’s been trouble with my husband’s sister. She’s been working things through the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to make it sound like it’s nothing, or smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for more than a year now.
Do you feel that your husband’s sister is acting on her own, or do you believe she is part of a larger plan or group working against you?

I think it’s mostly her doing it, but it’s through the family business, so other people get pulled into it or go along with it. I can’t say there’s some big group, but she’s been trying to get control of the money and keep me out of decisions. People act like I’m making too much of it, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, since this situation with your husband’s sister started?

I don’t know that I’d say I’m hopeless or anything like that. It’s upsetting, sure, and I think about it a lot, but I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things like that. I’m mostly just bothered by what’s going on.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious, restless, or on edge a lot of the time because of this situation?
I mean, I get bothered by it, yes. I wouldn’t say I’m on edge all the time, but when something happens with the business or her name comes up, I do feel tense and it stays on my mind.
Have you ever felt that things are happening that others don’t seem to notice, or that you know something is true even though others say it isn’t?

Yes. That’s what I’ve been trying to explain. My husband’s sister has been working things through the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. Other people act like I’m reading too much into it or try to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for more than a year now.
Have you ever felt that people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you in ways beyond what’s happening with your husband’s sister?

No, not really beyond her. I don’t feel like strangers are watching me or anything like that. It’s about my husband’s sister and the family business—how she’s been working things to get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People try to make it sound like it’s nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Have you ever felt that you are being singled out for special treatment, or that you have a special role, mission, or identity that others don’t understand?

No, I wouldn’t say I have some special role or mission. It’s not like that. I came because of what’s been going on with my husband’s sister and the family business. She’s been working things so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and people keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for more than a year.

Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that other people don’t seem to share or understand, even though you know they are true, outside of what’s going on with your husband’s sister and the family business?

No, outside of that, I don’t think so. It’s really about my husband’s sister and the family business. She’s been working things to get control of the money and push me out, and people keep trying to make it sound like I’m overreacting, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on a long time now.
Even though others have told you that your concerns about your husband's sister may not be accurate, do you still believe strongly that she is working against you in this way?

Yes. I know other people keep saying maybe I’m reading too much into it, but I don’t believe that. She’s been working things in the family business to get control of the money and keep me out of decisions. I’ve been seeing it for more than a year now, so yes, I still believe it.

Even when people you trust have told you that your concerns about your husband’s sister might not be accurate, do you still believe that she is trying to take control of the family business and push you out of decisions?

Yes, I do. I know they think they’re helping by saying maybe it’s not what I think, but I’ve been watching this for over a year. She’s trying to get control of the money in the family business and keep me out of decisions. I know what I’ve been seeing.
Even though there may be no clear proof that your husband's sister is trying to take control of the family business and push you out, do you still believe this is happening?

Yes. I know people keep saying there isn’t clear proof, but I don’t need them to smooth it over for me. I came here because she’s been working that family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. I’ve been seeing it for more than a year now.
Even though there is no clear evidence that your husband's sister is trying to take control of the family business and push you out, do you still believe this with absolute certainty?

Yes, I do. I know I’ve said it already, but I’m sure of it. She’s been working things in that family business to get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. People can try to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year.

His sister has been working her way into the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. People can try to smooth it over, but this has been going on for more than a year.

inference.note: The patient maintains a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (about the husband's sister conspiring to take control of the family business and push them out) in the absence of other prominent psychotic symptoms, mood symptoms, or anxiety symptoms that would suggest another primary disorder. The belief is not better explained by another condition such as major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, or a personality disorder. This is consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).

opening_question.intent: Greet the patient and identify the primary reason for their visit.
opening_question.question: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent delusional belief that her husband's sister is scheming to take control of the family business and push her out of decisions, despite lack of evidence and others' reassurances. The delusion is non-bizarre, circumscribed, and has persisted for over a year. There is no evidence of prominent hallucinations, mood episodes, or broader psychotic features to suggest alternative diagnoses.
